To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dynamics of wood formation and xylem structures of European beech are similar at two temperate forest stands with different climatic conditions, and the onset, duration, and end of xylary cell differentiation steps and xylem-ring widths differ between the two sites.
the onset, duration, and end of xylan formation phases differed between two sites, but the time spans between successive wood formation phases are similar.

the dynamics of xylary differentiation processes in Fagus sylvestica L. are similar at different sites, but the duration of cell differentiation steps is shorter in the high elevation forest, and that vessel characteristics differ between the first and the last quarter of the xylary increment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the plasticity of wood formation and the development of vessels in F. sylvatica under different environmental conditions.
the dynamics of xylary differentiation in F. sylvatica and the effects of weather conditions on vessel characteristics in two temperate sites.
the plasticity of the xylemic system of F. sylvatica and the influence of environmental conditions on its development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

xylem formation in F. sylvatica L., at the two study sites, was not significantly affected by precipitation, but was influenced by other factors (i.e., temperature, photoperiod and hormonal regulation).
, although the duration and timing of xylem development differ, xylem formation processes in beech are highly similar between years and sites.

, although the duration of the major cell differentiation phases differed between the sites, the dynamics of xylary development in F. sylvatica was not affected by precipitation, but by the onset of cell production and the cessation of cambial activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the onset and end points of cell differentiation phases in F. sylvatica were not affected by the local weather conditions.
the xylem differentiation dynamics in European beech are not affected by the precipitation, which is not a limiting environmental factor for xylematic growth in beech.

the onset and end times of xylem cell differentiation processes in F. sylvatica are similar across different European sites, whereas the duration of xylem development is site-specific and depends on the onset of cell production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the duration and time span between successive phases of xylem development are similar in trees growing at two different sites, despite the different environmental conditions and tree-ring widths.

xylem formation processes and conduit characteristics are highly sensitive to environmental conditions, and the observed differences in xylem characteristics between the study sites may have implications on tree physiology and wood quality.
the timing of xylem cell differentiation and vessel characteristics are highly site specific.
